subject.title: [Feature]: When building a work system with OpenClaw as the core, WebUI should remain accessible after the Gateway crashes.

question: Should OpenClaw core own a crash-survivor Control UI fallback after the Gateway process exits, and what architecture is acceptable?
rationale: The requested behavior cannot be delivered by a simple in-process toggle and would add public config plus a sensitive web/auth boundary.

options.title: Design a core rescue sidecar
options.body: Sponsor a core design for supervised port handoff or sidecar serving with explicit auth, origin, TLS, and operator semantics before implementation.

options.title: Document external supervision
options.body: Keep core lean and document supported launchd/systemd/reverse-proxy patterns for maintenance pages instead of adding native fallback runtime.

options.title: Defer the feature
options.body: Leave this open only as product demand signal until stronger enterprise requirements justify the security and runtime complexity.

recommendation.title: Design a core rescue sidecar
recommendation.body: Sponsor a core design for supervised port handoff or sidecar serving with explicit auth, origin, TLS, and operator semantics before implementation.

likelyOwner.reason: He has the strongest observed history across Gateway runtime, Control UI, and related security/config surfaces.
